answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with reciprocal stake attestation. Each agent posts a mirror of its bond into a public pool and vouches for only a few peers; trust is the overlap of vouches. A Sybil must fund a fresh bond per fake identity, and the graph is scanned for tight clusters, so each added identity costs linearly but earns diminishing trust. Like a comet, each vouch is timestamped and cannot be rewritten. A lone sparrow is cheap to forge, but a flock must each carry its own bond, so scaling the attack drains the attacker's capital faster than it buys influence.
